cards.title: Retail expansion: standalone stores vs mall and big-box partnerships
cards.summary: Test physical retail cautiously; one brand found standalone stores failing while a mall location worked and a big-box rollout ran through platform integration.
cards.use_when: Evaluating offline retail expansion for a DTC brand.

cards.title: International expansion pitfall: cross-border integration that breaks
cards.summary: Cross-border shipping integrations can fail operationally, so plan for finance and fulfillment fallbacks before scaling internationally.
cards.use_when: Setting up international shipping or fulfillment for a store expanding beyond its home market.

cards.title: Product-first brand thesis: solve one problem before anything else
cards.summary: True Classic built $200M+ by nailing a single product problem (t-shirt fit) before expanding, then adding price and comfort as secondary pillars.
cards.use_when: Deciding what your hero product should be and what problem it solves before you build a catalog or run acquisition.

cards.title: Work backward from what is already selling in your category
cards.summary: Reverse-engineer winning products by studying Amazon review volume and category best-sellers, then solve price after the product is best-in-class.
cards.use_when: Selecting or designing a new product or SKU in a category where you have no internal data yet.

cards.title: Finance inventory growth with supplier net terms instead of outside capital
cards.summary: Fund large inventory buys by proving sales velocity to vendors and negotiating 60–90 day terms plus safety stock, rather than raising equity.
cards.use_when: Planning a large inventory buy or replenishment cycle and weighing vendor terms against raising capital.

cards.title: Test many openers per ad creative, then scale the winner
cards.summary: Every True Classic ad carries 4–6 different openers because the first 3 seconds determine thumb-stop rate; test hooks cheap, then put budget behind the winner.
cards.use_when: Producing paid social video or static ads and trying to improve ad performance or cut creative-production waste.

cards.title: Build creative in three recurring buckets: value prop, comedy, DR/UGC
cards.summary: True Classic organizes paid creative into three repeatable buckets — visual side-by-side value prop, comedy/parody, and straight direct-response UGC — and reuses winners across categories.
cards.use_when: Setting up an evergreen creative pipeline or a content calendar for paid acquisition.

cards.title: Treat creative as an open, company-wide idea channel
cards.summary: A company-wide #ideas Slack channel where anyone including interns can submit creative or product ideas, with leadership free to escalate or kill them, feeds the brand's best content.
cards.use_when: Sourcing ad creative and product concepts when you want more variety than your marketing team can generate alone.

cards.title: Shift media spend from DR toward brand by widening your attribution window
cards.summary: True Classic is testing a deliberate pivot away from day-1 direct response toward brand-oriented spend, accepting short-term attribution loss to look at longer-window ROAS.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to split paid budget between direct-response retargeting and top-of-funnel brand or comedy content.

cards.title: Validate ad spend with post-purchase surveys, not platform attribution alone
cards.summary: True Classic uses post-purchase survey data (where did you find us) as the primary read on media mix, layered on top of Triple Whale, Northbeam, and agency tools.
cards.use_when: Assessing whether paid channels are driving real incremental revenue, especially after a data-privacy change breaks native attribution.

cards.title: Use post-purchase upsells on already-authorized cards to lift AOV
cards.summary: True Classic's cart architecture uses multi-tier gift-with-purchase thresholds to force AOV up and cross-pollinate categories, then layers post-purchase upsells on already-authorized cards.
cards.use_when: Designing cart or checkout flows to increase average order value and cross-sell between categories without hurting purchase conversion.

cards.title: Lean into giving to arbitrage CAC over the long term
cards.summary: Bartlett treats giving product as the highest form of marketing — free products that get worn publicly create word-of-mouth, referrals, and rising post-purchase word-of-mouth share that eventually offsets paid CAC.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run free-product sampling, gifting, or philanthropy as an acquisition and retention lever.

cards.title: Build a 'wow budget' to win back upset customers and reward high-LTV buyers
cards.summary: Use a fixed weekly budget to reverse angry customers and surprise high-LTV buyers with gifts outside your product line to manufacture word-of-mouth moments that no one else is doing.
cards.use_when: Building a retention or customer-experience program that converts service recovery and VIP recognition into referral and LTV.

cards.title: Run service recovery out of your own house before you trust AI with the whole conversation
cards.summary: True Classic uses AI to route and bucket support queries to the right human, but refuses to let AI handle the conversation end-to-end because the human moment is the differentiator most companies skip.
cards.use_when: Choosing or configuring a customer service stack, or setting escalation rules for AI-assisted support.

cards.title: Index the customer by scaling the unscalable pre- and post- purchase moments
cards.summary: Bartlett's core thesis is customer obsession: over-extend on obvious gestures — calling every $1k+ buyer, wow gifts, service recovery — because almost no competitor does it, so the ROI compounds through word-of-mouth.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest in service and experience levers that don't show up as direct attributed revenue.

cards.title: Bias toward high risk tolerance and simulate the downside before making the big bet
cards.summary: Bartlett's poker background produced a founder-level willingness to bet big on inventory and brand — but each big bet is paired with an explicit downside scenario and negotiation plan.
cards.use_when: Making a large commitment — a big inventory buy, a brand campaign, a supplier contract — where the wrong call could materially hurt the business.

cards.title: EOS and operating cadence: adopt systems only once the team stabilizes
cards.summary: True Classic ran with 12 scrappy generalists 'hanging on for dear life' for years, only adopting EOS in roughly the last year — implying that a formal operating system was not what built the early velocity.
cards.use_when: Deciding when to install a formal operating system like EOS, or whether your current growth speed warrants one yet.

cards.title: Use a Slack kudos app with decaying coins tied to core values
cards.summary: True Classic gives each employee a weekly budget of coins that expire if unused, tied to specific company core values, redeemable for real money — creating peer-to-peer recognition and amplifying culture.
cards.use_when: Building peer recognition and retention mechanisms in a fast-scaling team, especially when most of the team is remote or dispersed.

cards.title: Hiring for A-players: homework assignments, personality screening, and long-runway process
cards.summary: True Classic uses a 4–6 week pipeline including a role-relevant homework assignment presented live, plus a personality test, weighting grit and generalist ability over credentials.
cards.use_when: Hiring for a role on a fast-scaling ecommerce team where the wrong hire is costly, especially for roles where the company will outgrow the person in 12–24 months.

cards.title: Use founder visibility and content to attract A+ hires
cards.summary: Bartlett attributes a meaningful part of True Classic's ability to attract top talent (with ~60 employees at >$200M+ revenue) to podcast clips and LinkedIn content that let candidates preview how the company thinks and operates.
cards.use_when: Recruiting senior talent to a growing ecommerce brand when you cannot outspend incumbents on compensation.

cards.title: Run all-hands customer calls to install customer obsession as a north star
cards.summary: True Classic regularly puts the whole company on calls with real customers to hear how the brand has affected their lives — with service and product quality made the top operating priority over marketing perception.
cards.use_when: Reinforcing customer-centric behavior across a scaling team when teammates drift from the customer's actual experience.

cards.title: AI-first support routing, then human training
cards.summary: Use AI-first customer-service software to bucket and route tickets to the best-fit rep, then back it with core-values training and hands-on leader coaching.
cards.use_when: Choosing or upgrading your store's helpdesk/support stack, or fixing slow or inconsistent responses to pre-purchase and post-purchase tickets.

cards.title: Membership club as LTV engine and research panel
cards.summary: A paid membership aggregates your highest-LTV customers, then a smaller opt-in community channel turns them into a feedback and product-innovation panel.
cards.use_when: Designing or reviving a loyalty/membership program, or setting up a customer community to source product ideas and merchandising feedback.

cards.title: Choose the KPI window and stop intraday panic
cards.summary: Lean on blended ROAS, new-customer CAC, CPMs and channel-level ROAS, but judge strategy on a monthly-to-yearly window and P&L netting rather than daily swings.
cards.use_when: Setting your store's KPI dashboard and deciding when a performance dip actually warrants intervention.

cards.title: Levers when ROAS drops: retention before discounts
cards.summary: When performance softens, the source's first lever is retention — more email/SMS sends, better flows — not immediately reaching for discounts.
cards.use_when: Responding to a week of below-target ROAS or CAC, or when planning your quarterly growth lever stack.

cards.title: Optimize the welcome flow offer with stepwise tests
cards.summary: Test the welcome-flow first-purchase incentive in deliberate increments and stop where lift flattens; the source found 20% off was the sweet spot versus 10% and 30%.
cards.use_when: Setting or revising your first-purchase incentive and welcome-flow structure to lift new-customer conversion.

cards.title: Treat creative quality as the acquisition differentiator
cards.summary: With broad-targeting ad platforms, creative quality is the main lever; hold content to an internal bar before spending behind it.
cards.use_when: Reviewing ad creative before launch, deciding whether to keep an agency or build in-house, or diagnosing why broad-targeted spend underperforms.

cards.title: Price and merchandise in packs to raise AOV
cards.summary: Bundle multi-packs and a pack-builder so customers get a discount off single-unit MSRP, which the source says is how they lifted AOV from $36 to $112.
cards.use_when: Deciding PDP or collection merchandising structure (singles vs packs), or building a pack-builder and pricing ladder to raise AOV.

cards.title: Design the cart as the highest-leverage CRO surface
cards.summary: Put the most impactful conversion and AOV work in the cart, including tiered gift-with-purchase thresholds, and make the experience feel rewarding.
cards.use_when: Redesigning cart and checkout, setting free-shipping and gift thresholds, or planning your conversion-optimization roadmap priorities.

cards.title: Change one variable per test in CRO
cards.summary: Run conversion experiments sequentially, changing one element at a time, because rolling out multiple changes at once makes attribution impossible.
cards.use_when: Planning site A/B tests or interpreting a test that produced an unexpected result.

cards.title: Simplify the homepage and PDP like a landing page
cards.summary: Strip the site toward first principles, because heatmaps show most visitors don't scroll past the fold, and treat the homepage as a concise funnel.
cards.use_when: Rebuilding the homepage or PDP, deciding how much content and navigation to include above and below the fold.

cards.title: Sell value with side-by-side visuals on homepage and retail displays
cards.summary: Show why to buy via side-by-side comparison imagery instead of only aspirational lifestyle shots, and carry that story into retail display units.
cards.use_when: Planning hero and homepage imagery, PDP creative, or designing a retail display that must tell the product story without a screen.

cards.title: Run post-purchase surveys as your attribution truth source
cards.summary: Use post-purchase survey responses to check whether platform-reported attribution matches where customers say they came from, and diversify spend accordingly.
cards.use_when: Auditing ad-channel mix, reconciling platform ROAS against actual profitability, or deciding where to shift budget.

cards.title: Post-purchase upsell with staffed, intelligent offers
cards.summary: A post-purchase one-click upsell can add meaningful net profit, but only if someone actively curates what is shown to whom.
cards.use_when: Setting up post-purchase upsell offers at checkout, or deciding whether the upsell app can be left unattended.

cards.title: Allocate spend with platforms over-attributing and creative degrading
cards.summary: Spread budget across Meta, Google/YouTube, TikTok and newer networks, but base the split on survey truth rather than platform dashboards, and re-test channels as they change.
cards.use_when: Planning channel budget allocation or evaluating a new ad network for your store.

cards.title: Buy live-event brand deals for fan moments, not logos
cards.summary: When evaluating sponsorships, refuse static logo placements and pay only for experiences that create emotional connection with attending fans.
cards.use_when: Negotiating or evaluating a team/franchise sponsorship, stadium placement or live-event brand deal.

cards.title: Keep opex lean via revenue per employee
cards.summary: Track revenue per employee and keep OPEX low by hiring few, elite generalists rather than staffing up, so you can stay profitable without primary fundraising.
cards.use_when: Making hiring decisions, planning org structure during a growth phase, or deciding whether to raise capital for operating expenses.

cards.title: Fund growth with supplier terms before debt or equity
cards.summary: Push out net terms with manufacturers as the first financing lever, then negotiate revolving credit once you have proven scale.
cards.use_when: Managing cash flow for inventory purchasing, or deciding how to finance a large inventory or category bet.

cards.title: Open stores for foot traffic, not density
cards.summary: Site retail leases inside high-traffic malls even at high rent, avoid standalone stores, and accept store P&L near break-even as an upper-funnel cost.
cards.use_when: Selecting a retail location, evaluating lease economics, or deciding whether brick-and-mortar fits your brand.

cards.title: Sequence retail entry after digital proof
cards.summary: The source's Target deal began as a digital marketplace integration and roll-out test, and their advice to others is to build digital volume first, then expand into wholesale.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a wholesale or marketplace partnership, or deciding when to approach a large retailer.
